messages.text: packing checklist bana do please, 2 bed flat shift kar rahi hoon. kahan se shuru karun

Start with rooms you use least: guest room, storage, books and seasonal clothes. Leave the kitchen and daily essentials for the last two days. A rough order:
1. Books, décor, off-season clothes
2. Spare linen, guest room
3. Most of the kitchen (keep 1 pot, 2 plates)
4. Bathroom and daily clothes on the last night
boxes kitne lagenge roughly?
For a two-bedroom flat, people usually need 35-50 medium boxes, plus 5-10 large ones for bedding and pillows. Book boxes are best kept small so they don't get too heavy.
ok. movers maine book kar liye hain btw, Al Bayt Movers, 3 June subah 8 baje
Great. Ask them whether they bring wrapping for furniture and whether they disassemble beds, so you know what to prepare. It also helps to label every box with the room it goes to.
haan label to karungi. colour coding karun?
Colour coding works well: one colour per room, and a matching sticky note on each door in the new flat so the movers know where to put things.
nice. aur ek baat, Lubna ko ghalat bata diya tha, rent 58 nahi 55k hai. 58 mein parking thi jo maine nahi li
Got it. If you're budgeting for the move, also set aside something for the first month's utilities and any building move-in fee.
hmm ok. STC ka internet bhi transfer karwana hai shifting se pehle, yaad rakhna
Call STC about a week ahead; transfers can take a few days. You might also consider hiring a cleaner for the old flat on the 4th so you get your deposit back without stress.
cleaner nahi, khud kar lungi. last cheez: fragile glasses kaise pack karun
Wrap each glass in paper, stuff the inside too, and stand them upright in a box with cell dividers. Fill gaps with towels and mark the box FRAGILE on every side.
perfect shukriya 🙏

messages.text: quick refresher: how did IFRS 16 change lease accounting vs IAS 17?

Under IAS 17, lessees split leases into finance leases (on balance sheet) and operating leases (just an expense). IFRS 16 removed that split for lessees: almost all leases now go on the balance sheet as a right-of-use asset and a lease liability. The expense becomes depreciation plus interest, so EBITDA usually goes up. Short-term and low-value leases can still be expensed.
ah yes. and lessors?
Lessor accounting barely changed: they still classify leases as finance or operating, much like IAS 17.

messages.text: go question: is it safe to close a channel from the receiver side?

Generally no. The convention is that the sender closes the channel, because sending on a closed channel panics. If several goroutines send, coordinate with a sync.WaitGroup and close the channel from a separate goroutine once all senders are done. Receivers can detect closure with `v, ok := <-ch`.
